description: A sixteen-step sequencer with three rows, each step tuned in semitones, quarter tones or twelfth tones

params.text: Sets the tempo of the internal clock, from 20 to 220 beats a minute; a step is a sixteenth of a beat
Sets how many steps the sequence runs before it starts again, from 1 to 16
Moves the whole sequence in whole octaves, three either side of the base note
Chooses the note the whole sequence is measured up from, the twelve semitones from C to B
Sets what A above middle C is tuned to, from 432Hz to 448Hz, which moves the whole sequence with it
Chooses the size of one step of a pitch knob: a semitone at CHROMATIC, half of one at QUARTER, or a sixth of one at TWELFTH
Chooses whether the sequence runs from the knob above or from the jack beside it
Starts and stops the sequence; with it off the outputs hold whatever they last carried
Sends the sequence back to its first step on each press
Sets that step's pitch for that row, 0 to 17 steps above the base note in whatever size the tuning switch is set to
Turns that step's trigger on and off for that row

inputs.text: Advances the sequence by one step on each rising edge, when the clock switch is set to EXT
A rising edge sends the sequence back to its first step

outputs.text: A one-sample pulse of 5V at the start of each step whose button is on for that row
That row's pitch for the step now playing, at 1V per octave

notes: the pitch outputs are measured from A at 0V, where most oscillators in Rack take 0V as middle C, so a sequence sounds nine semitones below the note names on the panel.
tuning the receiving oscillator up by nine semitones puts the note names back where the panel says they are.
the trigger outputs are a single sample long rather than a gate, so anything that expects a gate of some length will not follow them.
the three rows share the step count, the clock and the tuning; only the pitches and the triggers are separate.
a lamp above each column shows which step is playing, and the lamp by the play button shows that the sequence is running.
the pitch is clamped to four octaves either side of A, so a high base octave and a high step can run into that ceiling.
with the clock set to INT the sequence runs whether or not anything is patched; the external clock jack is read only when the switch is on EXT.

outputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
outputs.3: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
